'''2009 2K Event''' was a Players Committee event in Blue Bell, Pennsylvania, on 27–29 March 2009, recreating the 2000 World Championship: a Jabba's Palace sealed deck team event on 27 March, then a two-day constructed main event on 28–29 March in the [[Premiere - Death Star II]] format (Decipher cards only).<ref name="pc-news57">[https://web.archive.org/web/20090413053951/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/news/news.php?id=57 Worlds 2K Event – Penn. March 27-29, 09 – From Chris Fanchi] (2 April 2009), swccgpc.com. Internet Archive capture 13 April 2009.</ref> The main event drew 40 players and cut to the top 12 "as it was in 2000".<ref name="pc-news54">[https://web.archive.org/web/20090413000450/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/news/news.php?id=54 Worlds 2000 Event, Day 2 Qualifiers], posted by CRingwell (28 March 2009), swccgpc.com. Internet Archive capture 13 April 2009.</ref><ref name="pc-news57" /> The deck sheets below are transcribed from the Players Committee's scanned decklist PDFs ([[:File:2009 2K Event Day 1.pdf]], [[:File:2009 2K Event Day 2.pdf]]). The forum calls it the 2009 2K Event (Premiere to Death Star II); [[Hayes Hunter]] won and [[Justin Desai]] was runner-up.<ref name="f-2kresults">[https://forum.starwarsccg.org/viewtopic.php?t=26608 uh, results?], Kim Caton, Star Wars CCG Players Committee Forums, forum.starwarsccg.org (31 March 2009).</ref><ref name="f-2kfinals">[https://forum.starwarsccg.org/viewtopic.php?t=26558 finals], Michael Dalton, Star Wars CCG Players Committee Forums, forum.starwarsccg.org (29 March 2009).</ref> The Players Committee forum board for the weekend was titled "2009 Players Championship", and the announcement of the main event's legal sets called it the "2009 Player's Championship Weekend".<ref name="f-2kboard">[https://forum.starwarsccg.org/viewforum.php?f=386 2009 Players Championship (Past Event)], Star Wars CCG Players Committee Forums, forum.starwarsccg.org (forum board, topics January–April 2009). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20211006184725/https://forum.starwarsccg.org/viewforum.php?f=386 Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="f-2klegal">[https://forum.starwarsccg.org/viewtopic.php?t=25346 legal sets], Chris Gogolen, Star Wars CCG Players Committee Forums, forum.starwarsccg.org (30 January 2009).</ref> [[Scott Lingrell]] ran the event: he posted its FAQ, format and pre-registration list, named its tournament director and bought the mugs and the winner's trophy.<ref name="f-2kfaq">[https://forum.starwarsccg.org/viewtopic.php?t=24994 Worlds 2000 FAQ - March 27-29th, 2009], Scott Lingrell, Star Wars CCG Players Committee Forums, forum.starwarsccg.org (12 January 2009). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20210126111807/https://forum.starwarsccg.org/viewtopic.php?t=24994 Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="f-2kprereg">[https://forum.starwarsccg.org/viewtopic.php?t=25004 Pre-registration and Payment info.], Scott Lingrell, Star Wars CCG Players Committee Forums, forum.starwarsccg.org (12 January 2009).</ref><ref name="f-2ktd">[https://forum.starwarsccg.org/viewtopic.php?t=25067 Tournament Director], Scott Lingrell, Star Wars CCG Players Committee Forums, forum.starwarsccg.org (16 January 2009).</ref><ref name="f-2kpopcorn">[https://forum.starwarsccg.org/viewtopic.php?t=26403 Getcha Popcorn Ready!!!!], Scott Lingrell, Star Wars CCG Players Committee Forums, forum.starwarsccg.org (22 March 2009).</ref> [[Lee Edwards]] was the tournament director.<ref name="f-2ktd" /> It was held at Alternate Universes, 1530 DeKalb Pike, Blue Bell.<ref name="f-2kfaq" />

[[Scott Lingrell]] first announced a March 2009 event in the Worlds 2000 format on 15 October 2008. After talking with the players in charge of the Match Play Championship, he wrote, two separate events would be run: the [[2009 Match Play Championship]] on 3–4 January 2009 in Open constructed format, and a "Players Championship 2009" in March in the Worlds 2000 format, with $1000 guaranteed to the winner. The top four from each event were to meet in a separate eight-player event at Origins or GenCon, with alternates used in order, for a $500 prize.<ref name="pcf-23548-341470">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=341470#341470 Player's Championship - March 2008, Worlds 2000 Format], Scott Lingrell (CRingwell), Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (15 October 2008). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20081021233924/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=342143&sid=198be8cdf7bda3b05cc740ccf203ad9f Internet Archive]</ref> Lingrell wrote that the format of that event "could be whatever. swiss/sealed/cube (or all three?)".<ref name="pcf-23548-341496">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=341496#341496 Player's Championship - March 2008, Worlds 2000 Format], Scott Lingrell (CRingwell), Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (15 October 2008). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20081021233924/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=342143&sid=198be8cdf7bda3b05cc740ccf203ad9f Internet Archive]</ref>

== Format ==

* '''Environment:''' [[Premiere - Death Star II]]
* '''Site:''' Blue Bell, Pennsylvania<ref name="pc-news57" />
* '''Venue:''' Alternate Universes, 1530 DeKalb Pike, Blue Bell<ref name="f-2kfaq" />
* '''Organizer:''' [[Scott Lingrell]]<ref name="f-2kfaq" />
* '''Tournament director:''' [[Lee Edwards]]<ref name="f-2ktd" />
* '''Dates:''' 27–29 March 2009 (team event 27 March; main event 28–29 March)<ref name="pc-news57" />
* '''Players:''' 40 (main event)<ref name="pc-news54" />
* '''Winner:''' [[Hayes Hunter]]<ref name="f-2kresults" />
* '''Runner-up:''' [[Justin Desai]]<ref name="f-2kresults" /><ref name="f-2kfinals" />

== Weekend schedule ==

The weekend had three events.<ref name="f-2ksched">[https://forum.starwarsccg.org/viewtopic.php?t=25807 Event Schedule], Kim Caton, Star Wars CCG Players Committee Forums, forum.starwarsccg.org (19 February and 24 March 2009).</ref>

* '''Friday 27 March, 6:30 pm:''' a [[Jabba's Palace Sealed Deck]] team event for teams of two, $4 a player, with a cut to a final confrontation and mugs for the winning team.<ref name="f-2ksched" /> [[Michael Dalton]] and [[Kim Caton]] finished 3rd.<ref name="f-2kfinals" />
* '''Saturday 28 March:''' Day 1 of the main event, eight games of Swiss constructed using only cards available at the 2000 World Championship, cutting to the top 12.<ref name="f-2kfaq" /><ref name="f-2kformat">[https://forum.starwarsccg.org/viewtopic.php?t=24987 Main Event Format, Swiss Event, $750 guarenteed - 1st place], Scott Lingrell, Star Wars CCG Players Committee Forums, forum.starwarsccg.org (12 January 2009).</ref><ref name="f-2ksched" />
* '''Sunday 29 March:''' Day 2, four games of Swiss for the top 12, then a final confrontation between the top two; players could change decks between the two days.<ref name="f-2kfaq" /> The top 12 received cash, and the schedule gave a World Championship bye to the winner and the runner-up. From 11 am the same day a constructed consolation event in the Worlds 2000 card pool offered cash and a World Championship bye to its winner.<ref name="f-2ksched" />

The cash prizes for the main event's top 12 were $750, $200, $75, $75, $50, $50 and $25 each for 7th to 12th places.<ref name="f-2kfaq" /> Any version of a legal card could be played, including foils, white- and black-bordered printings and the two oversized objectives; sleeves had to be opaque, and all current rules and errata applied.<ref name="f-2kfaq" />

== Day 1 qualifiers ==

The Players Committee posted the 12 Day 2 qualifiers with their scores, and two alternates, after Day 1 (28 March 2009).<ref name="pc-news54" /><ref name="f-2ktop12">[https://forum.starwarsccg.org/viewtopic.php?t=26553 Top 12 for day 2], Scott Lingrell, Star Wars CCG Players Committee Forums, forum.starwarsccg.org (29 March 2009).</ref> Scott Lingrell's forum post of the same list gave 40 players in total.<ref name="f-2ktop12" /> Earlier wiki text gave the site as Philadelphia.

[[Chris Fanchi]]'s report, posted on the PC site, adds that the final was [[Hayes Hunter]] against [[Justin Desai]], that Fanchi finished 4th, and that [[Mike Richards]] won the consolation event on 29 March. In the 27 March team sealed deck event Hayes Hunter and [[Brian Rippetoe]] beat Fanchi and Mike Richards in the final confrontation.<ref name="pc-news57" /> In that event each player received one [[Jabba's Palace Sealed Deck]] and each two-player team four [[Cloud City Limited|Cloud City]] packs to add to the five Jabba's Palace boosters; only one set of the sealed deck premiums could be used, an ECC Lando replaced [[Lando With Vibro-Ax]], ability-1 characters had ability 2, and characters ignored location deployment restrictions. About seven or eight teams played. After the Swiss rounds Fanchi and Richards were the first seed and Hunter and Rippetoe the second; the winners received mugs.<ref name="pc-news57" />

In the main event Fanchi was 5th after Day 1 with 11 (+66), and Mike Richards was 15th, the third alternate. Six of the twelve Day 2 qualifiers had played [[Ralltiir Operations / In The Hands Of The Empire|Ralltiir Operations]] on Day 1, and many players used Ralltiir Operations and [[Mind What You Have Learned / Save You It Can|Mind What You Have Learned]]. Fanchi played Ralltiir Operations and EBO X-wing decks taken from [[Brian Hunter]]'s DeckTech page, changing only a few cards.<ref name="pc-news57" />

== Day 2 final standings ==

[[Kim Caton]] announced the final standings at the end of the event. Her list after the event gave the places below; she marked 5th and 7th to 11th as uncertain.<ref name="f-2kresults" /> In the final [[Hayes Hunter]] beat [[Justin Desai]]; Hunter won the first game with his [[Ralltiir Operations / In The Hands Of The Empire|Ralltiir Operations]] deck by 17.<ref name="f-2kfinals" />
